title: Benny Carter, "the King"
summary: Budd rates Benny Carter among the greatest altos and tells a story of Phil Harris saying Carter scored his wife's films and played parts for the men.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Just a last name -- Benny Carter. He's a ______.

Carter, they called him King, the King, because -- I'll tell you a little story about this. I had never heard nobody in the world playing alto saxiphone like Benny Carter, and he had such a beautiful, beautiful, fluid, flowing style. And so one day, you know, like when Billy Eckstine was trying to tell me about Charlie Parker before I really knew who Charlie Parker was, Billy said, man, this cat --and he used Benny Carter 25 a, uh -- he said, this cat plays more than Benny Carter, because he couldn't think of nobody else. I'll say, impossible. Nobody in the world can play as much saxiphone as Benny Carter. He said, Budd, you gotta hear him.
Well, I still say they were just two great saxophone players. I couldn't say who was greater than the other, and really, because -- well, I look at music, I have to take a
whole general look, all around look. Now, of course, Benny Carter's tone take, for instance
And he was more academic, would you say?
Oh, Benny Carter knew everything. One time when I was writing for Tony Paster, and I was in the regular band for Tony Paster --
Well, I had mentioned that I had written for Tony Paster.
Yes. Yes, it's on there somewhere.

Anyway -- I think it's back on the other page, Mel. Anyway, when I was writing for Tony Paster, we were -- I went up -- we were in the Paramount theater here in New York, and so I said, after -- well, I wasn't playing in the band, but I had to be there every day because I'm the arranger, you know, and sometimes we'd rehearse between shows. So after one of the shows, I went to Tony Paster's room. I used to go into his dressing room all the time and talk to him. When I went into the room, there was Phil Harris. Phil Harris had come by to see Tony Paster. So like I'm the only Black cat in the room, so like, you know, Phil -- Phil is a

pretty cool cat. So I mean he wanted -- probably had something to say to me, and he said, do you know Benny Carter? I say, oh, sure. I said, I know Benny Carter very well, he's a good friend of mine. He says, let me tell you something. He said, I didn't know he was the kind of musician that he is. I say, oh, I thought everybody knew Benny Carter was a musician. He said, this man scores all my wife's pictures, Alice Faye, you know. He said, he's just finished scoring a picture, and he says that when the cats can't play the part on an alto, he picks it up and play it for them to show how it goes.
